notes.body: Bōya is an affectionate way of addressing a very small child, though literally it suggests a boy; the child here has been introduced as a little girl.
An aluminium pot, a Western-style table, and beef stewed with potato mark a poor but modern city household of the period.
The Japanese, natsukashimi, means a warm, longing fondness for what is past, held here together with forgiveness and peace.
The baby's babble also sounds like the Japanese word for tasty, good-good.

data.say: Kept four sparse notes for what the English cannot carry alone; left vision, that day, and storm frame unnnoted per reading.
